title: Substituent effects in the formation of aryloxide-bridged europium complexes

synthesis.procedure: Under nitrogen, a europium ingot (0.193 g, 1.27 mmol) and 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol (0.527 g, 2.55 mmol) were combined in a Schlenk flask with a magnetic stir bar. Liquid ammonia was condensed into the flask at -41 °C using a dry ice–acetonitrile bath and condenser; the characteristic blue metal–ammonia color was observed. After about 6 cm3 of liquid ammonia were collected, the vessel was removed from the cold bath and ammonia was evaporated to a canary yellow powder. The vessel was placed under dynamic vacuum for 5 min and brought into a glovebox. Unreacted 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol (66 mg, 0.3 mmol) was removed by hexane extraction. The remaining yellow solid was extracted three times with 4, 2 and 1 cm3 of MeCN, centrifuged, and rotary-evaporated to give 1 as a yellow powder (0.858 g, 93% based on Eu; the printed milligram unit is inconsistent with the reported yield and formula mass). X-ray quality crystals were grown from MeCN over 7 d at ambient temperature in the glovebox.
synthesis.temperature: -41 °C for NH3 condensation; ambient temperature crystallization
synthesis.time: NH3 condensation then evaporation; 5 min dynamic vacuum; crystals grown over 7 d
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk flask under nitrogen; liquid-ammonia condensation with dry ice–acetonitrile bath; glovebox workup
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Hexane extraction of unreacted phenol; MeCN extractions (4, 2, 1 cm3), centrifugation and rotary evaporation; crystals from MeCN over 7 d at ambient temperature in the glovebox.
synthesis.yield: 0.858 g, 93% based on Eu (printed as 0.858 mg)

properties.summary: Evans-method magnetic susceptibility of 1 is consistent with divalent europium (μeff = 7.8 μB at 298 K). Weak UV/VIS absorptions were recorded in MeCN; no luminescence data were reported for the isolated complex.

synthesis.procedure: A europium ingot (0.740 g, 4.86 mmol) and 2,6-diisopropylphenol (1.74 g, 9.76 mmol) were combined as described for 1. The blue metal–ammonia color was observed initially, but a yellow solid precipitated within 3 min of ammonia condensation. After about 10 cm3 of liquid ammonia were collected, the vessel was removed from the cold bath and ammonia evaporated to a yellow powder. Dynamic vacuum for 5 min changed the color to orange. In the glovebox the orange powder was extracted with hexanes to remove unreacted 2,6-diisopropylphenol (45 mg, 0.25 mmol). The solids were dried and extracted with 6, 4 and 2 cm3 portions of hot MeCN and centrifuged to an orange solution. Rotary evaporation yielded 2 as an orange powder (0.532 g, 92% based on Eu). X-ray quality crystals were grown from MeCN over 2 d at ambient temperature in the glovebox.
synthesis.temperature: NH3 condensation as for 1 (dry ice–acetonitrile bath); hot MeCN extraction; ambient-temperature crystallization
synthesis.time: yellow solid within 3 min of NH3 condensation; 5 min dynamic vacuum; crystals grown over 2 d
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk flask under nitrogen as for 1; liquid-ammonia condensation; glovebox extraction
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Hexane extraction of unreacted phenol; hot MeCN extractions (6, 4, 2 cm3) and centrifugation; rotary evaporation; crystals from MeCN over 2 d at ambient temperature in the glovebox.

properties.summary: The Evans-method moment of 2 (μeff = 7.4 μB at 298 K) is consistent with Eu(II). A UV/VIS absorption at 344 nm in MeCN was reported; no luminescence of the isolated cluster was measured.
